answer_1.quote: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) enjoys tremendous success... In this work, we present a systematic study of different kinds of hallucinations, studying them through the lens of generalization, memorization and optimization in sequence to sequence models.

answer_2.quote: We then compare the hallucination behaviour under perturbation of the most-memorized samples with random samples using the hallucination detection algorithm... We report results using chrF, BLEU as well as the prediction accuracy... BLEU is used for test evaluation... The NH estimator uses LASER similarity scoring.

answer_4.quote: Manual detection of hallucinations, however, is an impediment for fast experimental cycles, and in this work, besides explaining the generation of such natural hallucinations... we also propose an approximate corpus level hallucination detection algorithm to aid faster analysis. ... we manually ascertaining whether an output generated is hallucinated or not.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators manually assess whether a generated translation is a hallucination (severely inadequate) or not.
